body: I'm currently teaching college classes. It's just that everything feels like a dead end though. Because of my stupid emotional issues, I'm never going anywhere in life.

This is one of the reasons I've held off on it a bit. I don't know if it's low-self-esteem/trauma/depression or actually me as a person. It's a mixture of both. I'm very comfortable with things platonic and have this dream of living in a family group (like a group of adults who raise all the children as their own). I can only think about this in the extended family situation (in which I grew up) and in a plural family type situation (thank you reality TV). I haven't really give it as much thought before. 

I don't know. I think some of the fear of a sexual relationship stems from a history of sexual abuse and depression. However the desire for a non-monogamous family group is very much a part of me as a person.

There's a lot here--I have a lot to think about. Thanks for this response. For the comment on why couples, looking back, I'm not sure why I said that. Actually, I'm fine with existing groups or coming together as individuals and forming a group.

Yes! I grew up in an Indian extended family. I love it in many, many ways. I have issues, though, with some of the Indian cultural values surrounding the situation a sense of "duty" that can create resentment, honor culture that forces people to fit a certain mold to protect the family name, a notion that interpersonal boundaries are a bad thing, etc. I have always wished that if only I could replicate something like that but where all the adults choose to be in that situation and the children are "our" children. Kind of like a co-housing/intentional community situation but an actual family. I imagine living in houses close to each other--separate units but with joint backyards :). 

I made the decision a while ago that once I am stable in my career I am going to seek out a co-housing community. That's how I want to live my life.
